input: fuel_blend_map_correction_weighted (call 1) and fuel_boost_map_correction_weighted (call 2): each is map_fuel_correction_factor (the selected manifold pressure: boost_pressure_sensor_value, boost_pressure_target or the sensor default, chosen by cm848_selectLoadNormalizer) x a filtered blend weight >> 8
output: fuel_blend_compensation_target / fuel_boost_compensation_target, read only by fuel_demand_blend_compensate / fuel_demand_boost_compensate (0x504b0c / 0x504eb0), which form error = (filtered fuel demand - fuel_demand_compensation_base_setpoint) - target and step a compensation integrator with it
units_check: x axis 422..32188 (10 breakpoints, the last two equal) is in units of map_fuel_correction_factor (0.0159 inHg per count) x weight >> 8; the weight scale is not confirmed, so only the monotonic concave shape was checked; values 2240..12928 are in the units of the filtered fuel demand minus its base setpoint (not independently confirmed)
evidence: Both lookups share this table pair and both outputs are subtracted from (filtered fuel demand - base setpoint) in the two compensate functions, which also use the 0x4071e0 / 0x40720c curve on the same two quantities (weighted correction >> 2 against that curve of the demand), so this table is its pressure-to-demand partner.
naming_concern: The inputs are manifold-pressure based (map_fuel_correction_factor); the word map is kept out of the name to avoid the abbreviation. The output scale reaches 12928 while the forward curve input is clamped at 5760, so the pair is not an exact inverse and the name states the role only.

input: rpm_load_table_result (call 1, positive gain) and throttle_load_offset_working = 0xb400 - rpm_load_table_result (call 2, negative gain): a blend angle in 1/256 degree, 0..46080 = 0..180 degrees
output: throttle_load_gain_positive = table(angle) and throttle_load_gain_negative = table(180 degrees - angle), Q13 gains used in cm848_calculateLoadAdjustmentFactors: throttle_rate_control_input = positive x throttle_fuel_demand_scaled >> 14 - negative x throttle_rate_integral_input / 0x51ec and throttle_rate_filtered_sum = the two cross terms
units_check: x axis 0..46080 in steps of 2560 (19 points, 10 degrees each at 256 counts per degree) is exactly the 0..0xb400 domain of the angle; the values equal 8192 x cos(angle / 2) at all 19 points (largest error 3.3 counts of 8192), 8192 = 1.0 at 0 degrees falling to 0 at 180 degrees
evidence: The two lookups pass an angle and its complement (0xb400 - angle) through one table and the table is a half-angle cosine, so the pair is cos(angle / 2) and sin(angle / 2): a cos / sin weighting of the two signals; the numeric fit of all 19 values is within 0.04 percent of full scale.
naming_concern: The throttle_* names of this cluster (0x10f68-0x11400) are doubtful: throttle_position_scaled is (fuel_demand_rate_limited - fuel_quantity_ema_filtered) / 2, a fuel demand deviation, not a throttle position; the family prefix is kept only so a later cluster rename catches these tables too.

input: throttle_position_scaled, set in cm848_processLoadAdjustment to (fuel_demand_rate_limited - fuel_quantity_ema_filtered) / 2: the deviation of the rate-limited fuel demand from its filtered value (signed axis)
output: throttle_position_accumulator, a Q13 gain (not an accumulator), used in cm848_calculateLoadBasedAdjustment as throttle_fuel_demand_scaled = (gain + throttle_position_increment) x throttle_position_scaled / 8192, clamped to +-25600
units_check: x axis -959..384 counts, 64-count steps in the middle (one count is 2 fuel counts; assuming the 0.0679 mm3 fuel scale for fuel_quantity_ema_filtered, which was not independently confirmed, that is 0.136 mm3, so +-127 = +-17 mm3 and 384 = 52 mm3); values are Q13 gains: 8192 (1.0) from -127 to 128, rising by 2048 per 64 counts to 16384 (2.0) at +-384, symmetric
evidence: The result multiplies the same deviation that indexed the table (plus an optional load increment), so the table is a gain curve on the fuel demand deviation: unity inside +-17 mm3 rising to 2.0 beyond +-52 mm3.
naming_concern: throttle_position_accumulator holds a Q13 gain, not an accumulator or a position; throttle_position_scaled is a fuel demand deviation, not a throttle position.

input: sensor_readings_t_0040baf2.barometric_pressure (ambient pressure, sensor slot 3, AMB SPN 108, 0.0159 inHg per count)
output: result x 256 -> governor_cold_start_iat_correction, step-limited by governor_cold_start_band_cal and written to the dword at 0x40aec8 (governor_output_t_0040aec2.governor_output_high), which cm848_calculateProtectionSpeedLimits compares with governor_speed_limit_active as candidate 9 (the idle speed target, base 6000 = 750 rpm); when governor_iat_correction_enable_cal is nonzero the same two tables are read by index with a pressure hysteresis instead of interpolated
units_check: x axis 0, 943, 1443, 1446, 1886 = 0, 15.0, 22.9, 23.0, 30.0 inHg at 0.0159 inHg per count (1886 is just above standard atmosphere, the 1443 / 1446 pair is a step at 23 inHg); values all 6000 x 0.125 = 750 rpm, the same base as governor_speed_limit_active
evidence: The table output is one candidate in the highest-wins selection of governor_speed_limit_active (governor_output 9), whose base is 6000 = 750 rpm, and the table is flat at 6000, so it is an idle speed by ambient pressure (altitude compensation); the barometric input is the named sensor field.
naming_concern: Destination governor_cold_start_iat_correction (0x3faf80) is misnamed: the input is barometric pressure, not intake air temperature (stale from the old .intake_air_temp slot name), and the variable is write-only (the live copy is the dword at 0x40aec8); governor_iat_correction_enable_cal and governor_iat_correction_mode_enable_cal carry the same stale iat label.

input: x = intake_air_heater_start_temperature (1/64 deg F, signed; intake manifold temperature else coolant, taken once after reset); y = protection_iat_scaled = barometric_pressure x protection_iat_scale_factor_cal / 100, latched once by cm848_processSensorTemperatureData
output: intake_air_heater_preheat_total_ticks: total grid heater preheat ticks; 0 sets intake_air_heater_no_preheat_flag and clears logical output requests 43 / 44, otherwise it seeds intake_air_heater_preheat_remaining_ticks and starts the heater
units_check: x axis -2566..5126 = -40.1..80.1 deg F (12 breakpoints, step pairs at 0 / 15 / 66 / 80 deg F); y axis 1257, 1446, 1572, 1697, 1823 = 20.0, 23.0, 25.0, 27.0, 29.0 inHg at 0.0159 inHg per count (barometric); grid 0 / 100 / 150 / 300 ticks (300 at 0 deg F or less, 150 up to 15 deg F, 100 up to 66 deg F, 0 above; 0.1 s per tick per the CSV note), first and last pressure rows identical
evidence: Input x, input y and the output are all named and traced, the y breakpoints are round barometric pressures and the grid reproduces the documented preheat schedule; the call sits at the top of cm848_computeIntakeAirHeaterPreheatDuration.
naming_concern: protection_iat_scaled is scaled barometric pressure, not an intake air temperature (stale label from the old .intake_air_temp slot name); a later rename should drop iat from it.

input: x = engine_rpm_state_t_0040b7ac.current_rpm (0.125 rpm per count); y = engine_load_input_b, a copy of engine_timing_reference (a fuel quantity, 0.0679 mm3 per count) written by engine_injectionAngle_selectCylinderInjector
output: throttle_rate_lookup_raw -> (replaced by fuel_demand_mode_select_cal when throttle_rate_override_flag = 1, clamped to throttle_output_clamp_lower_cal..upper_cal) -> returned by cm848_lookupRpmLoadTable into rpm_load_table_result (cm848_processLoadAdjustment), the angle of the L057 half-angle cosine gain tables
units_check: x axis 0..28800 = 0..3600 rpm; y axis 0, 147, 294 ... 2061, 2355 = 0..140 mm3 in 10 mm3 steps then 160 mm3 (fuel quantity); the grid is 46080 (0xb400, the end of the 0..0xb400 angle domain of the half-angle cosine table) at every point, so the gains are fixed here: positive 0, negative 1.0
evidence: cm848_calculateLoadAdjustmentFactors uses rpm_load_table_result and 0xb400 - rpm_load_table_result as the two angles of the cosine table, and this grid holds the value 0xb400, so the grid is an angle by engine speed and load (fuel quantity); the physical purpose of the blend is not identified.
naming_concern: rpm_load_table_result and throttle_rate_lookup_raw are an angle (1/256 degree), not a throttle lookup; engine_load_input_b holds a fuel quantity (a copy of engine_timing_reference); the throttle_* family prefix is kept for a later cluster rename.

input: x = cm848_calculateBoostPressure() (boost = intake manifold pressure above barometric, 0.0159 inHg per count); y = engine_rpm_state_t_0040b7ac.current_rpm; computed only when engine_feature_enable_flags_cal bit 0x100 is set
output: injection_timing_demand_floor, a lower bound applied to injection_timing_demand in the injection timing arbitration (it raises the demand to the floor, sets torque_limit_arb_t_0040a2f6.source_priority = 0xb and clears timing_arbitration_status_bits)
evidence: Both inputs are named sensor quantities with round-number breakpoints and the output is compared as a minimum against injection_timing_demand, so the destination name is accurate.

input: x = engine_rpm_state_t_0040b7ac.current_rpm; y = sensor_readings_t_0040baf2.coolant_temp (1/64 deg F, signed)
output: oil_pressure_model_unfiltered -> exponentialMovingAverage -> engine_oil_pressure; with oil_pressure_switch_only_cal set (this truck) the switch alone can force it to 0, otherwise it is the dash oil pressure
units_check: x axis 0, 5200, 12000, 20000, 28000 = 0, 650, 1500, 2500, 3500 rpm; y axis -1280, 0, 7040, 12480, 15680 = -20, 0, 110, 195, 245 deg F; grid 0..9216 counts at 1/18.56 kPa per count = 0..497 kPa (72 psi): cold row (-20 deg F) 0, 375, 419, 483, 497 kPa, hot row (245 deg F) 0, 207, 303, 331, 359 kPa = 30..52 psi from idle to rated speed, a realistic oil pressure curve
evidence: The result is the engine oil pressure model of cm848_processEngineOilPressure (the function comment and firmware/CLAUDE.md both describe an RPM-indexed model on this truck) and the hot / cold pressures fit a real engine.

input: x = cooling_fan_speed_target (radiator_fan_speed scale, 0.125 rpm per count); y = engine_rpm_state_t_0040b7ac.current_rpm
output: cooling_fan_feed_forward_duty, added to the PD term x 16 and the integral term in cm848_runCoolingFanSpeedPid and clamped 0..25600 into cooling_fan_duty_request
evidence: The lookup output is summed with the PID terms and clamped to the duty request range 0..25600, so the destination name is accurate, and both axes fit the fan target / engine speed scales.
naming_concern: cooling_fan_feed_forward_table, the first call argument, is the lookup cache (interpolation state), not the table.

input: x = engine_rpm_measured (0.125 rpm per count); y = fuel_pressure_feedback_filtered (rail pressure feedback, 0.0488 MPa per count)
output: injection_timing_table_offset, added to the per-cylinder base angle DAT_0005fbb2[cylinder_event_index] (and in one place injection_timing_cam_angle_correction) and wrapped modulo 0x7800 to form the TPU injection angles (e.g. injection_angle_ch6_crank_position)
units_check: x axis 0, 8000, 16000, 24000, 48000 = 0, 1000, 2000, 3000, 6000 rpm; y axis 0..4098 in steps of about 410 = 0..200 MPa in 20 MPa steps; grid 803..855 counts, falling with speed (855, 846, 838, 829, 803 from 0 to 6000 rpm), first and last pressure rows identical (no pressure dependence in this calibration); the angle unit follows the 0x7800 wrap, so no degrees are claimed
evidence: The output is added to a per-cylinder angle table and wrapped at 0x7800 in three TPU angle computations, so it is an angle offset that depends on engine speed and rail pressure; the angle unit and the physical reason are not identified.
naming_concern: The destination injection_timing_table_offset is vague: it is a crank angle offset added per cylinder (modulus 0x7800), not a timing demand, and the word table in it adds nothing.

input: x = engine_rpm_state_t_0040b7ac.current_rpm (0.125 rpm per count); y = sensor_readings_t_0040baf2.coolant_temp (1/64 deg F, ET1 SPN 110)
output: cold_start_fuel_demand_min_floor: the lower bound of the integral in fuel_coldStart_integralCorrection_update, a PI fuel demand limit that runs only while cold_start_overheat_active_flag = 1 (set by engine_coolant_overheat_check with coolant_overheat_temp_threshold as setpoint) on error = cold_start_coolant_temp_setpoint - coolant_temp; fuel_coldStart_demandMin_2dLookup also raises cold_start_fuel_demand_pi_correction to it (reason code 2), and the limit feeds protection_fuel_limit_active
units_check: x axis 4000..28000 = 500..3500 rpm (21 breakpoints); y axis 14336, 14464, 14592, 14656, 14720, 15040, 15360, 15552, 15808, 16320 = 224, 226, 228, 229, 230, 235, 240, 243, 247, 255 deg F, the overheat range, and 255 deg F (0x3fc0) is also the setpoint default while the flag is off; grid 1030..2134 counts = 70..145 mm3 at 0.0679 mm3 per count: 2134 at every speed for 224 deg F, and at 255 deg F falling from 2134 at 1000 rpm to 1030 from 2000 rpm
evidence: The loop is gated by an overheat flag, regulates coolant temperature against a latched overheat threshold, and the y axis covers only 224..255 deg F, so this is the minimum fuel the overheat derate may command, not a cold start value.
naming_concern: The cold_start_* and fuel_coldStart_* names around 0x5139b8-0x513ddc (cold_start_fuel_demand_min_floor, cold_start_fuel_demand_pi_correction, cold_start_fuel_demand_ramp_output, cold_start_overheat_active_flag) describe a coolant overheat fuel derate, not a cold start; the destination name was not copied for that reason.
